3.16.22.en: "Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms maketh an atonement for sins" (Sir 3:28). "Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations" (Lk 16:9). "But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you" (Lk 11:41) [26].

3.16.23.en: St. Jerome He who repays a kindness with a kindness thinks of the future, and in the day of his fall he finds a support [29].

3.16.24.en: v I ask you that we not speak evil against our teachers, nor call them to account in strictness, lest we bring evil upon ourselves. Let us examine ourselves, and not speak evil of others. Let us honor that day on which we were enlightened (by Baptism). Whoever has a father, whatever his faults, let us cover them all. For it has been said: "Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father's dishonour is no glory unto thee... and if he lose his understanding, be longsuffering with him" (cf. Sir 3:10-13). If this was said about our fathers according to nature, how much more regarding our spiritual fathers. Honor him because every day he serves you, and reads the Holy Bible to you, and prepares lodging for you, for all his worship is on your account [27].

3.16.25.en: St. John Chrysostom Inspired by Sirach 3

3.17.s.en: Sanctify my family as Your church

3.17.0.en: v Your descent to our earth has sanctified all our life.

3.17.1.en: You make of my heart a holy temple for You, and of my family a church of Your own, indeed of the whole world a new heaven rejoicing in Your presence!

3.17.2.en: Glory to You, who hold the children of men dear!

3.17.3.en: v You instill in every leader the spirit of fatherhood or motherhood toward others.

3.17.4.en: So he lives cherishing his younger brothers. He does not pick up their weaknesses or faults, but learns from every person what builds himself up, and regards his presence among men as a constructive divine gift!

3.17.5.en: v What concerns me is the salvation of the whole world.

3.17.6.en: In a spirit of hope I await the day of the Church's meeting with You on the clouds.

3.17.7.en: I see all believing humanity, from Adam to the end of the ages; I take pride in being a member of Your family, which You cleansed with Your precious blood, and sanctified by the guidance of Your Holy Spirit over it.

3.17.8.en: v Train me with all my brothers in the language of heaven and its constitution.

3.17.9.en: Let my tongue speak the sweet word to old and young, and let my heart meditate on true love for the good and the bad, and let my will go forth in harmony and submission to Your divine will.

3.17.10.en: I offer honor to my parents and my brothers and my children.

3.17.11.en: I see all of them on the way, wearing the garment of Your righteousness.

3.17.12.en: And the heavenly beings marvel at the beauty of Your bride, humanity.

3.17.13.en: The heavenly beings rejoice because their prayers for us, since the first man, have borne fruit in splendor and beauty for mankind.

3.17.14.en: v It does not concern me to bury my father at his death (Lk 9:49-60); or to bid farewell to my family in order to follow You (Lk 9:61-62); but that we all go forth together on our journey to heaven with Your presence in us!

3.17.15.en: v If anyone grows old or is struck with loss of memory, I will deal tenderly with him, reckoning that what has befallen him may befall me.

3.17.16.en: What I deal out to them will be returned to me one day. What I offer them, I offer to You, O Lover of mankind.

3.17.17.en: v You descended, O fearsome Lord, to the human family.

3.17.18.en: You became for us a model of meekness and humility of heart. May we be united with You, and taste the greatness of meekness in our family life.

3.17.19.en: St. Mary did not exalt herself that she was the only one chosen as Your mother.

3.17.20.en: But by Your incarnation from her she grew in humility through You. Grant us that whenever our success increases by Your grace, we may rise with more humility.

3.17.21.en: Whenever we receive honor in the family or the Church or the world, adorn our souls by multiplying humility and meekness.

3.17.22.en: May every member realize that his honor is from the honor of his brothers.

3.17.23.en: Let us learn from Archbishop John Chrysostom, who feared pride for himself, and used to repeat:

3.17.24.en: I marvel at a bishop who is saved!

3.17.25.en: O priest, you are the father of all humanity.

3.17.26.en: O bishop, there is no episcopate without a people!

3.17.27.en: Grant us all this mind, full of love, meekness and humility!

3.17.28.en: v As a member of the holy human family, grant me not to think beyond my capacities (2 Cor 12:6).

3.17.29.en: I do not seek dry rational knowledge that I may boast of it.

3.17.30.en: Nor do I desire to perform a miracle or work a surpassing sign.

3.17.31.en: Paul confessed that he knows in part, so shall I count myself possessed of knowledge and learning?!

3.17.32.en: He was caught up to the third heaven, and counts himself the chief of sinners.

3.17.33.en: So what shall I call my wretched soul?!

3.17.34.en: Grant me that You keep me in the faith, and that I not seek what exceeds my ability.

3.17.35.en: I do not search into Your divine essence, but I cast myself into Your embrace.

3.17.36.en: I do not ask how Your eternal birth was accomplished, but I melt with love for the Spirit of adoption which You have given to believers!

3.17.37.en: I am not concerned with knowing the ranks of the heavenly beings, but I fly with joy at joining their wonderful choir.

3.17.38.en: v In You and by You I enjoy my membership in the family.

3.17.39.en: You are the divine Father of the family.

3.17.40.en: The head of the whole family, which includes the heavenly orders and the congregation of believers!

3.17.41.en: I thank You for the knowledge You have given me about Your mysteries.

3.17.42.en: And I praise You for what You hide from me for my edification.

4.0.s.en: 1. Our responsibility toward the needy as toward the great

4.0.0.en: 1 My son, do not deprive the poor of his living, and do not make the eyes of the needy wait. 2 Do not grieve the hungry soul, and do not provoke a man in his need. 3 Do not add more trouble to the provoked heart, and do not delay giving to him who is in need. 4 Do not refuse to give the wretched his request, and do not turn your face away from the poor. 5 Do not turn your eye away from the needy, and do not do anything that brings upon you the curse of man. 6 For if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his Maker will hear his prayer. 7 Be affable to the congregation, and bow your head to a great man. 8 Bend your ear to the poor, and answer him gently and meekly. 9 Deliver the oppressed from the hand of the oppressor, and be not fainthearted in judging. 10 Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of a husband to their mother; 11 so you will be as a son of the Most High, and He will love you more than your mother does.

4.0.1.en: "My son, do not deprive the poor of his living, and do not disappoint the looks of the needy" [1]. It is stated in the Didache, or the Teaching of the Lord to the Gentiles by the Twelve Apostles (4:5-8): [Do not stretch out your hands to receive, and close them when giving (Sir 4:31). If you have anything through the labor of your hands, give a ransom for your sins (by giving). Do not hesitate to give, and when you give do not grumble, for you will know who is the good Rewarder. Do not turn away the needy, share everything with your brother (Acts 4:32-37). And do not say that you have anything of your own. For if you share in the things that are immortal, how much more in those that are mortal? (Rom 15:27)]. 1. Giving is for living, not for luxury and comfort [1]. 2. If the believer is unable to give materially, he does not blame the poor man or rebuke him [2]. 3. Giving is not appraised by quantity and money, but by its practice with joy, and he does not delay the needy man [3]. 4. He fixes his eyes not on what he will give, but on the heart of the needy man, so that both may enjoy salvation [4]. 5. He gives the poor man what he needs, and offers honor to those to whom honor is due [7]. 6. He gives the needy man a sweet word that lifts up his spirit [8]. 7. The believer behaves without partiality toward a rich man or a man of authority [9]. 8. As a son of the Most High, the believer opens his heart to all, imitating his heavenly Father [10].

4.0.2.en: My son, do not deprive the poor of his living, and do not disappoint the looks of the needy [1].

4.0.3.en: When we meet a poor man we remember that God has given us goods as a deposit that we return to Him, and as His children we imitate Him by giving generously, and enter into friendship with Him and cleave to Him.

4.0.4.en: v What need is there to mention the virtues of this craft and its excellences? It teaches you how to become like God, and this is the head of all good things.

4.0.5.en: v Almsgiving is strong and has authority, so that it looses bonds and chains, and dispels darkness, and quenches the blaze of the fire of Gehenna, and its effectiveness qualifies one to become like God, as He said: "Be merciful, as your Father who is in heaven is merciful."

4.0.6.en: v Mercy raises man to a lofty height, and gives him eloquent boldness before God.

4.0.7.en: For just as when a queen wishes to enter the king's place, none of the courtiers dares to prevent her or ask her where she wishes to go, but all of them receive her with rejoicing, so he who practices mercy and almsgiving appears before the throne of the King without hindrance, for God loves mercy exceedingly, and she remains near Him; therefore the Scripture said: "Upon thy right hand did stand the queen." This is because mercy is preferred by God, since it made Him become man for our salvation.

4.0.8.en: v Nothing makes us so near to God and in His likeness as this good work!

4.1.0.en: St. John Chrysostom Do not grieve the soul of the hungry, and do not anger a man in his despair [2].

4.1.1.en: As it is fitting to offer food to the man who is hungry in body, we must offer hope to the man whom despair is crushing. Instead of rebuking him for his gloomy outlook full of deadly despair, we support him with the spirit of hope, the giver of joy amid afflictions. We bear witness to the tenderness of the Savior, who forgives sins, whatever our sins may be.

4.1.2.en: v Question: Does he fall into despair of his salvation who has been caught in many evils, and sinned after his baptism? Or what is the measure by which a man may continue in his hope in the love of God for mankind through repentance?

4.1.3.en: Answer: If you can balance the surpassing tenderness of God, or the weight of the greatness of God's mercy, against the number of sins and their weight, there is no room for despair. But if it is reasonable that the latter is subject to measure and number, while it is impossible to measure God's mercy or count His tenderness, there will never be any place for despair. Rather, by the knowledge of mercy and the condemnation of sins, there is forgiveness in the blood of Christ, as it is written (Mt 26:28).

4.1.4.en: Yet there are many places and ways through which we learn that we must not despair. Consider especially the parable of our Lord Jesus Christ concerning the son who took his father's wealth and squandered it in sins. From the words of the Lord Himself we learn what kind of feast, and how great, is fitting for repentance (Lk 15:22-24).

4.1.5.en: Add to that God's saying through Isaiah: "Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool" (Isa 1:18). This is fulfilled when our repentance deserves it, if it proceeds from our hatred of sin, as it is written in the Old and New Testaments, and bears fruits worthy of it [1].

4.2.0.en: St. Basil the Great Do not add more trouble to the provoked heart, and do not postpone your gift to the needy [3].

4.2.1.en: Postponing giving to one who is truly in distress stirs anxiety in his soul, so we add to his material need his deprivation of inward peace.

4.3.0.en: Do not turn away the suppliant in his distress, and do not turn your face away from the poor [4].

4.3.1.en: The needy man looks not only at the gift you give him, but gazes at your face to see whether he sees in it the icon of God, who gives generously and cheerfully.

4.3.2.en: v It is not enough to show mercy, but it is fitting that we offer it generously, with a bountiful spirit, and not only with a bountiful spirit but with a joyful and cheerful spirit... (The Apostle) stressed this same point strongly when he wrote to the Corinthians to urge them to generosity, saying: "He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully" (2 Cor 9:6). And to correct their mood he says: "not grudgingly, or of necessity" (2 Cor 9:7)... For if you grieve while you are showing mercy, you are harsh and violent.

4.3.3.en: If you are sad, how can you support those who are in sorrow?...

4.3.4.en: This is the reason for his saying: "He that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness" (Rom 12:8), for how can he be sad of countenance who receives the Kingdom?!

4.3.5.en: Who remains sad of countenance while he receives the forgiveness of his sins?

4.3.6.en: So do not think of your spending of money (the work of mercy) but of the abundance you receive through the spending. For if he who sows rejoices although he sows uncertain about the harvest, how much more he who tills the heavens? For you give only a little to receive much... By the two mites the widow was reckoned to have surpassed those who offered many talents, because of her generous spirit [2].

4.4.0.en: St. John Chrysostom Do not turn your gaze away from the needy, and do not give a man an opportunity to curse you [5].

4.4.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serug calls us to receive the Lord Christ through our meeting with the poor and needy. And we reckon that what we offer of love and concern we offer to the Lord Christ Himself. It is a wonderful opportunity to express our honor to the Lord Himself.

4.4.2.en: v By these works of righteousness which you give him, he asks you to receive him with joy.

4.4.3.en: If you give him a crust of bread and a cup of water, let your thought be joyful and with love.

4.4.4.en: He is weak and tired and distressed and tormented and coming to you, so give him lodging and rest, and rise and serve him gladly.

4.4.5.en: He is greatly tormented by poverty and bears sicknesses, so show him great love lest he be distressed.

4.4.6.en: Has he stood as a poor man at your door? God Himself has come to you, so open to him cheerfully that he may enter.

4.4.7.en: If he had come to you through a rich man you would be ashamed, and you would not be able to receive him.

4.4.8.en: He came and visited you in humility and lowliness, and when you fill his belly with bread you find life.

4.4.9.en: Give him of what is his, and do not give him of what is yours, for you have nothing to offer him of what is yours.

4.4.10.en: It is He who came, and through the poor He asks you to trade with the Kingdom in every case.

4.4.11.en: He gave you His body; offer Him bread because He is hungry, and you drink His blood, take and bring Him a drink because He is thirsty.

4.4.12.en: He gave you to put on brightness and splendor from the water, so do not withhold from Him ragged clothes and humble garments.

4.4.13.en: All that you give through the poor who ask you, He rewards you for with a garment of light in the new world [3].

4.5.0.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serug For if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his Maker will hear his prayer [6].

4.5.1.en: A man may despise the poor man through the features of his face, or the manner of meeting him, and the soul of the poor man groans without uttering a word, but his Maker looks upon the bitterness of his soul within, and responds to it.

4.6.0.en: Be beloved of the congregation, and bow your head to a great man [7].

4.6.1.en: If the Holy Scripture in both its Testaments is concerned with our meeting with the poor and supporting them materially, spiritually and psychologically, on the other hand we must offer honor to whom honor is due. "Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour" (Rom 13:7).

4.7.0.en: Bend your ear to the poor, and answer him words of peace with meekness [8].

4.7.1.en: Since the Word of God became incarnate and dwelt among us as one of us, He called us to learn from Him, saying: "Learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart" (Mt 11:29). Ben Sirach offers us practical touches for a life of meekness and humility for the believer to live out in his small family as well as in society as the greater family.

4.8.0.en: A. Meekness does not stop at certain words or actions, but it is fitting that it be blended with and shine forth in all the works of man [17].

4.9.0.en: B. The believer does not seek worldly honor, but whenever he receives honor or authority or success in his works it is fitting for him to grow in humility, reckoning that what he receives is free gifts from God, so he finds favor with the Lord, and honor even from men [18].

4.9.1.en: C. It is fitting for the believer not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think (Rom 12:3), but to know the truth of his abilities and capacities. So he does not seek what is impossible for him, nor inquire into hidden matters with useless theoretical disputations [21-24]. When Pope Athanasius was asked by a man to show him his God that he might believe in Him, he answered him: "Show me your spirit, and I will show you my God!"

4.9.2.en: v Do not lower your tongue... fill it with blessing and the giving of abundant alms. For you can give alms even by speech. "Thus a word is better than a gift" (cf. Sir 18:16). And also: "Incline to the poor, and answer him words of peace with meekness" (cf. Sir 4:8) [4].

4.9.3.en: St. John Chrysostom v The divine voice counsels us in the language of the Holy Scriptures: "Honour the LORD with thy substance" (Prov 3:9)... The Lord says that the owner is you; and lest our souls be proud, He said: "Pay your debt" (Sir 4:8) [Vulgate]...

4.9.4.en: If a man is consecrated, he gives (to the poor) as from what is his own, and if he does not consecrate himself he is asked to return the money to its original owner, as though what he has were not his. God has truly established the Law, by the desire to give voluntarily, or by payment of necessity. God wishes to say: "Give if you wish, otherwise you will return it to the original owner upon refusing to give" [5].

4.9.5.en: Salvian, priest of Marseilles Deliver the oppressed from the hand of the oppressor, and be not a coward in judging in his favor [9].

4.9.6.en: It is fitting for the believer to realize that every ability he has is a gift from God on behalf of society as far as he is able, whether money or a position of leadership or authority or strength and health. All his life is turned into instruments of righteousness on behalf of the Kingdom of God, so if an opportunity is given him to do justice to the oppressed, but in his partiality to the oppressor for one reason or another he did not do justice to the oppressed, he is condemned for that. He may not show partiality to anyone because of blood kinship or his social position or wealth or nationality or religion or friendship with him, for God is a lover of all humanity.

4.9.7.en: v It may be said to one who has authority: Why do you not help the widow and orphans when injustice befalls them? Are you without strength? Can you not support them? I appointed you thus for this purpose, not that you may sin, but that you may prevent injustice [6].

4.9.8.en: St. Ambrose v Love must be equal toward all without partiality... For those who walk thus, blood relationship will not find room to offer greater love because of the tie of blood, as in dealing with a brother or son or daughter according to the flesh, so as to offer greater love because of the blood relationship than the love toward others. He who follows nature in these matters (that is, favoring relatives) gives clear testimony that he has not yet withdrawn completely from nature, but is still subject to the law of the flesh [7].

4.9.9.en: v Improper disputes and private love are alike; both must be removed from the monastery. For enmity arises from quarrels and private friendship and divisions that arise from suspicion and jealousy.

4.9.10.en: In every instance the loss of equality (in dealing) is the root and foundation of all envy and hatred on the part of those who are slighted. For this reason we received the Lord's command to imitate His goodness, who makes the sun rise on the just and the unjust (Mt 5:45). If He gives a share of light without partiality to all, so it is fitting for His followers to send forth the rays of love with equal splendor upon all alike.

4.9.11.en: But if "God is love" (1 Jn 4:16) as John says, then of necessity Satan is hatred. And just as he who has love has God in consequence, so he who has hatred embraces Satan within him [8].

4.9.12.en: St. Basil the Great Be as a father to the fatherless, and as a husband to their mother, and you will be as a son of the Most High, and He will love you more than your mother's love for you [10].

4.9.13.en: What occupies the believer's heart is not the quantity of the giving he offers, but that in all his conduct he be "as a son of the Most High," enjoying partaking of the divine nature (2 Pet 1:4).

4.9.14.en: v Let us look upon the poor as benefactors to us, able to offer us a fundamental principle for our salvation. And let us give generously and with a spirit of joy without delaying in our offering, but speaking to them with great reverence, showing great meekness (Sir 4:10) even before offering your gift, so you lift up his spirit from the gloom caused by his extreme need, by your gentle words. The Scripture says: "A word is better than a gift" (cf. Sir 18:16). For speech can lift up the spirit, and give rest [9].

4.10.0.en: 12 Wisdom brings up sons for herself, and takes to herself those who seek her. 13 Whoever loves her loves life, and those who rise early to her are filled with gladness. 14 Whoever possesses her inherits glory, and wherever she enters, there is the blessing of the Lord. 15 Those who worship her serve the Holy One, and those who love her the Lord loves. 16 Whoever listens to her judges the nations, and whoever attends to her dwells securely. 17 If he commits himself to her, he inherits her, and his descendants remain in possession of her. 18 For at first she walks with him by crooked ways; 19 she brings fear and dread upon him, and tests him with her discipline until she trusts his soul, and tries him with her judgments. 20 Then she returns and deals with him uprightly and gladdens him, 21 and reveals her secrets to him, and gathers in him treasures of knowledge and understanding of righteousness. 22 But if he goes astray, she forsakes him and delivers him to his ruin.

4.11.0.en: This poem personifies wisdom (that is, looks upon her as a person), reckoning her as a mother and those who seek her as sons. At the beginning wisdom allows the one who seeks her to enter into trials so that he may be proved, and declare whether he chooses wisdom or folly. And when he succeeds in the trial, wisdom declares to him her secrets, and as a divine teacher she teaches. 1. The believer begins his way with affliction in the company of God, the gladdener of hearts and revealer of divine secrets [17-18]. 2. He takes care that wisdom does not depart from him while he is on his way to eternity [19]. 3. Wisdom offers on the way her blessings, among them the following:

4.11.1.en: A. Pride in glorious sonship to God [11].

4.11.2.en: B. Love of the way of love and rising early to it [12].

4.11.3.en: C. Tasting the earnest of eternal glory [13].

4.11.4.en: D. The believer drinks from the Holy One the spirit of holiness and love [14].

4.11.5.en: E. He bears witness to God, and so judges the nations [15].

4.11.6.en: F. What concerns him is acquiring the wisdom of God Himself, for He is the giver of gifts, and at the same time offers Himself as a gift [16].

4.11.7.en: Wisdom exalts her sons, and takes to herself him who seeks her [11].

4.11.8.en: Since the believer is asked to be in the position of a father to the orphan and a guardian to the widow [10], he may feel unable to accomplish that with all his heart, so he asks that wisdom dwell in him, and so he bears the spirit of spiritual motherhood or fatherhood, by which he who possesses her longs to lift up others as his children, regardless of age. With his heart the believer embraces every man by the wisdom dwelling in him. We can say that Mother Wisdom is far from withdrawing from others; she embraces him who seeks her, and gives him of her characteristics, and he in turn embraces the hearts of others.

4.11.9.en: Those who seek her: The enjoyment of divine wisdom is not static, but requires growth in it, so we must seek her [11], and love her and rise early to her [12], and possess her, that is, take pride in her [13], and serve her [14] and obey her [15] and turn to her or devote ourselves to her [15] and trust in her and rely on her [16].

4.11.10.en: The wisdom that Ben Sirach praises is the one who truly deserves praise, the wisdom of God, that is, the Savior; whoever loves Him loves life at an eternal level. For the Lord Christ is the wisdom of God and the power of God (1 Cor 1:24). He magnifies His children who believe in Him, revealing to them by His Holy Spirit the divine mysteries, and gives them continual growth in knowledge, and fills their lives with the joy of the Gospel message. Whoever loves the incarnate wisdom of God loves life, for he keeps His commandments, and so receives eternal life (Jn 12:50). That is, he enjoys in the world the earnest of eternal life, as he experiences the life of constant inward joy. Thus is fulfilled in him the saying of Wisdom: "Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors. For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the LORD" (Prov 8:34-35).

4.11.11.en: Whoever loves her loves life, and those who rise early to her are filled with gladness [12].

4.11.12.en: Wisdom opens the heart with love as she opens the mind to holy understanding, so she reflects on the believer the spirit of gladness. Wisdom calls all, perhaps they will accept belonging to her, and become her sons, who seek her and she takes them to her fatherly bosom. In the Book of Proverbs we see wisdom lifting up her voice in every place, and calling everyone (Prov 5:1-21).

4.11.13.en: v In the first instance, while wisdom calls everyone, she calls the simple to understand with prudence, and the unlearned to use their hearts, so that the zealous and watchful reader may establish the meanings of the distinct and different words. She teaches that all things must be practiced and understood and praised and perceived according to their (sound) methods and plans [10].

4.11.14.en: St. Hilary of Poitiers Whoever possesses her inherits glory, and the Lord blesses whatever place she enters [13].

4.11.15.en: v Paul testifies that he was sent to proclaim a hidden wisdom which the great men of this world did not know, and therefore they are called foolish. The wisdom of God is hidden, because it is not in words but in power. It is impossible to set it forth in human expressions, but it is believed by the power of the Spirit. God foresaw the sins of the coming world and therefore established this wisdom in a manner baffling to those who want to turn His wisdom into their foolishness, and also to glorify us who believe in Him [11].

4.11.16.en: Ambrosiaster v The work of the Father which pervades all existence is glorified, and becomes exceedingly great when every man advances and reaches the highest stature of growth through fellowship with Christ "Wisdom" and "Knowledge" and "Holiness."

4.11.17.en: The same thing is accomplished when man is sanctified and purified and reaches the highest degrees of perfection through fellowship with the Holy Spirit, and thus becomes more worthy to receive the grace of wisdom and knowledge, so that all stains of defilement and ignorance are removed from him, and he reaches this progress in perfection and purity. Thus the life he received from God is worthy of God, that is, pure and perfect. So the creature deserves this (holy) life (after the likeness of the Creator); for the man whom the Creator wills for him receives from Him the power to exist eternally.

4.11.18.en: Origen Those who serve her serve the Holy One, and those who love her the Lord loves [14].

4.11.19.en: He who obeys her will judge the nations, and he who turns to her dwells securely [15].

4.11.20.en: The wise man who walks in the spirit of love and humility enjoys true discernment, and so understands the secret of the fall and rise of nations, and lives in confidence. He realizes how great empires collapse because of their pride, so he takes care for the spirit of humility and surrender into the hand of the Lord. The Book of Ben Sirach touches the Jewish tradition of prophecy which declares what lies behind historical events. The believer senses that historical events did not come haphazardly, but that God Himself is the governor of history with a purpose that surpasses human thought.

4.11.21.en: If he relies on her he inherits her, and his descendants remain in possession of her [16].

4.11.22.en: At first she walks with him in troublesome ways, and brings fear and dread upon him, she torments him with her discipline, until she trusts his soul and tests him with her judgments [17].

4.11.23.en: Divine wisdom is a free gift which the grace of God offers to the believer, so she allows the believer to enter into afflictions so that his soul may be purified, and he learns on the way of suffering in the company of the Crucified, and in this company he enjoys the risen life in Christ who rose from the dead.

4.11.24.en: v "If you do not return, He will sharpen His sword."

4.11.25.en: This he says by way of threat, to urge those slow to repent to return (conversion). He does not threaten immediately with wounds and blows and death, but sharpens weapons with a certain preparation as for vengeance.

4.11.26.en: By this action he points to attack as in a war. Therefore you long for a stop to God's movement toward vengeance; the Holy Scripture says that He sharpens His sword, He bends His bow, and makes it ready, and in it He prepares the instruments of death (Ps 7:13). The instruments of death are the powers that destroy the enemies of God.

4.11.27.en: "He makes His arrows fiery" (Ps 7:13). The Creator made fire for materials that burn. Certainly it was not made for steel, which does not melt in the fire, but for wood, which burns; so also God made arrows for souls that can be kindled...

4.11.28.en: Those, then, who were accepted beforehand, and held fast within themselves the fiery arrows of the devil, are those who receive the arrows of God. For this reason "He makes His arrows fiery."

4.11.29.en: Sensual love burns the soul, and so does the desire of the love of money, and fiery wrath, and sorrows that inflame the soul and melt it, and fears foreign to God. He who is not struck by the arrows of the enemy, and puts on the armor of God (Eph 6:11), remains unaffected by the arrows that bring death [12].

4.12.0.en: St. Basil the Great Then she returns to him directly and gladdens him, and reveals her secrets to him [18].

4.12.1.en: Ben Sirach spoke of those who wish to acquire wisdom that they are first exposed to testing and discipline, and if they pass the examination with patience, wisdom returns to them and gives them herself and becomes a guide for them, and offers them her secrets, so they enjoy a life of inward joy and gladness. Some see in this verse a hidden reference to the fall of Solomon the wise, though he returned and repented of his sins.

4.12.2.en: Then she returns to him directly and gladdens him, and reveals her secrets to him [18].

4.13.0.en: And if he goes astray she forsakes him, and delivers him to his ruin [19].

4.13.1.en: Some see that Solomon the wise speaks of his fall by the tongue of wisdom, which forsook him in his fall and then returned to him at his repentance: "Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded; but ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof... when your fear cometh as a storm, and your calamity cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: for that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD: they would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices. For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them" (Prov 1:24-32).

4.14.s.en: 3. The holiness of the universal family and being on guard against evil

4.14.0.en: 23 My son, observe the time, and beware of evil. 24 And do not be ashamed concerning your own soul, 25 for there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and grace. 26 Do not show partiality, for that is harmful to your soul. 27 And do not be ashamed with a shame that is your ruin. 28 Do not refrain from speaking in the time of salvation, and do not hide your wisdom when it is fitting to display it. 29 For wisdom is known by speech, and instruction by the utterance of the tongue. 30 Do not contradict the truth, but be ashamed of your ignorance. 31 Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not struggle against the current of the river. 32 And do not abase yourself to a foolish man, and do not show partiality to the face of the mighty. 33 Strive for the truth unto death, and the Lord God will fight for you. 34 Do not be harsh in your tongue, nor slack and negligent in your works. 35 Do not be as a lion in your house, and as a madman among your family. 36 Let not your hand be stretched out to receive, and closed when it should give.

4.14.1.en: As the believer guards against evil, he avoids the shame that prevailed in the Hellenistic world (Sir 5:13-6:1; 31:16-42:8). Ben Sirach distinguishes between the shame that evil brings, and the shame because of meekness that leads to honor. It is not fitting for the wise man to stop speaking wisdom at the right time for fear of false shame.

4.14.2.en: Observe the right time, and beware of evil, and do not bring shame upon yourself [20].

4.14.3.en: It is fitting for man to observe the right time. Now is the moment you are living, and are aware of, and are able to take the decision befitting you, and set out to carry out the decisive decision, but the coming moment is not yours, and you do not know whether you will be, in your consciousness, able to take the sound decision or not.

4.14.4.en: "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven" (Eccl 3:1). Our life with all its circumstances and conditions proceeds according to an ordered plan and design, so that God's purposes are fulfilled at the right time. We must perform our duties faithfully at the right time, and prepare for the future, to see God's plan for us. God created the world for our sake by a wonderful plan, and at the right time He sent the fathers and prophets and gave us the Law, and at the appointed time salvation was accomplished by the Cross, and with heavenly wisdom God cares for every small and great thing in your life, even the number of the hairs of your head does not escape His care.

4.14.5.en: In other words the history of the whole world and the history of your own life in particular, with all its minutes, are links of events that God arranges. You must live in a spirit of faithfulness, working with all your energies, and living with joy and gladness trusting in God who orders your life, for you by yourself cannot do anything whatever your desire and whatever your abilities.

4.14.6.en: Origen says: ["To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven." There is a time for gathering goodly pearls, and another time after gathering them for discovering the pearl of great price, when it is fitting for a man to go and sell all that he has to buy that pearl. For just as a man who wants to become wise in the words of truth must first learn the principles and then pass beyond through the elementary instruction, which he esteems with all esteem yet does not remain fixed at that point, but reveres it at the beginning of the matter and then seeks perfection. He acknowledges the favor for what he was taught at the outset, because it benefited him much! So the Law and the Prophets are understood with perfect accuracy as elementary teaching for the understanding of the Gospel in its fullness and the understanding of the meaning of all the words and works of Christ [13].]

4.14.7.en: If God as a Creator who loves mankind "hath made every thing beautiful in his time" (Eccl 3:11), and all that He created is good and by good ordering, yet He lifts us above time... He submitted to time in order to lift us above time, for He "has put eternity in their heart, without which man does not perceive the work that God does from the beginning to the end" (Eccl 3:11).

4.14.8.en: For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and grace [21].

4.14.9.en: Glorious modesty accompanies holiness, not the destructive shame before God [21]. St. John Chrysostom noticed in one of his homilies that those present were fewer than usual, and when he learned that the reason was the presence of a banquet of food before the meeting, the saint commented on the words of Ben Sirach: "For there is a shame that bringeth sin, and there is a shame which is glory and grace" (4:21), saying: It is not shameful for a man to share in the spiritual feast of the word of God after sharing in the feast of food. For the feast of the word of God has no fixed time; man may share in it whether he has previously partaken of food or his stomach is empty. The Apostle Paul says: "Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season" (2 Tim 4:2). Furthermore Luke the Evangelist relates to us that Paul, being ready to depart from Troas on the morrow, continued his speech until midnight, and a young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep, and fell down from the third loft (Acts 20:7-9). Chrysostom asked: [Was time a problem for him? Did time hinder him from continuing his preaching? [14]]

4.14.10.en: v "I have made your face hard like their faces, and your forehead hard like their foreheads" (Ezek 3:8). Just as shame is praiseworthy when confronting evil, it is blameworthy when used toward what is good. When the face reddens with shame because of evil, this is the work of the wise person, but the reddening of the face with shame because of doing good is a matter of folly...

4.14.11.en: He who is ashamed, repenting of an evil he committed, enjoys the freedom of life; and he who is ashamed of having done good falls from his upright position (1 Cor 10:12), and inclines toward the curse. And as the Savior says: "For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory" (Lk 9:26).

4.14.12.en: Some carry what is good in their minds, but since they are not confident in it they cannot defend the truth. He who is not afraid or ashamed to speak what he thinks uprightly is able to defend the truth [15].

4.14.14.en: v The shame that brings sin is a man's being ashamed to change his inclination to sin, lest he be accused of being fickle in mind or lest he be judged by his own testimony that he is mistaken [16].

4.14.15.en: St. Augustine Do not show partiality to anyone that harms your soul, nor honor toward another that leads to your fall [22].

4.14.16.en: In the service of fallen souls St. John Chrysostom demands that the servant of these souls be committed to bending down to take the fallen man by the hand on the ground and lift him up. But he must first plant his feet firmly on the ground, that he may lift his brother from the ground in safety, and not himself fall with his brother thrown on the ground.

4.14.17.en: Do not withhold a word in the time of need for it [23]. Ben Sirach warned us often of the slip of the tongue, and of the sin of idle talk or vain speech. This drives some to try to train themselves in silence. This training, to which the pious commit themselves, if used at an unsuitable time becomes evil silence. So when the believer feels the necessity of speaking at a suitable time for the edification of his brother, he is committed to speak. Just as there is evil speech, there is also evil silence; and just as there is holy silence there is also holy speech. The work of wisdom is to give the believer the spirit of discernment, so that he knows when to speak and when to be silent.

4.14.18.en: v You are the Word who gives a word to those who speak, through You all who speak speak for Your sake.

4.14.19.en: A ray and a radiance and a great light shone upon me that I might look at You. By my looking at You the soul is enlightened, and so acquires goodness.

4.14.20.en: And when the soul departs from You it is filled with darkness, and if it gazes upon You, it puts on light so as to speak the words of Your tidings...

4.14.21.en: Silence and speech stand over me and demand of me. O Lord, order my life according to Your will.

4.14.22.en: If I am silent I marvel, for I feel my insufficiency (for speech). Let me be silent in wonder, and not in vain arrogance.

4.14.23.en: And if I speak, may my word be according to Your glory and for Your sake.

4.14.24.en: When the soul is filled with silence in wonder at You, this silence is a discourse full of every benefit.

4.14.25.en: And if the soul is moved to glorify You with love... then I move by love, and I move to glorify You. And in wonder I am silent and do not cease from glorifying You.

4.14.26.en: Grant me, O Lord, wonder and word, that I may be enriched. And every day I wonder, and every day I move with speech!

4.14.27.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serug v Set, O Lord, a guard upon my mouth, and a strong door upon my lips" (Ps 141:3). He did not say: "a strong barrier, but "a strong door." For a door is opened as it is also shut. If this is a door, let it open and shut. It opens for the confession of sin, and shuts for the forgiveness of sin. For it is a door of safeguarding, not of destruction [17].

4.14.28.en: St. Augustine v In silence you see your mind, but when you use your mind, you speak within yourself. For during silence the mind begets the word, and the word of thanks that is offered to God is the salvation of man [18].

4.14.29.en: St. Anba Anthony the Great In a letter of Mar Philoxenus to the monks of Amid, which he wrote from his exile and in which he urged them to strive for the upright faith, he said in it:

4.14.30.en: [The monk who is silent about the faith is a hypocrite who does not know God...

4.14.31.en: The monk who is with everyone like him (changes color and conforms to everyone) is a hypocrite who wears the face of a devil.

4.14.32.en: The monk who puts on Christ and is silent about the truth, his garment is the leprosy of Gehazi.]

4.15.0.en: For wisdom is known by speech, and instruction by the word of the tongue [24].

4.16.0.en: Do not oppose the speaking of the truth, but be ashamed of your ignorance [25].

4.16.1.en: The good tongue is the holy tongue and the one under control. The wise man will not yield the truth, nor fear to confess his ignorance [25] or his sin [26].

4.17.0.en: Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not stand before the current of the river [26].

4.17.1.en: Truth resembles an unceasing current [25-26], so a man does not cover up his sins. Confessing a fault does not cause shame, but ignoring it in stupidity is the real shame.

4.17.2.en: v The lot fell upon (Jonah), and he became subject to accusation on the basis of fact. Perhaps he was afraid, but in truth the accusation became clear (and certain) by his confession. Therefore the wise counsel for those who wish to keep it is: "Be not ashamed to confess your sins" (Sir 4:26) [19].

4.17.3.en: St. Cyril the Great v It is necessary that we confess our sins to those to whom the stewardship of the mysteries of God has been given. Those who showed repentance in ancient times offered it before the saints. It is stated in the Gospel that they confessed their sins to John the Baptist (Mt 3:6), and in the Book of Acts they confessed to the Apostles by whom they were also baptized (Acts 19:18) [20].
